text_blocks.snippet: The "One Big Beautiful Bill," which extends provisions of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA), was passed by Congress and signed into law by President Trump in July 2025. It includes provisions such as no tax on tips and overtime, an increased child tax credit, and a new deduction for seniors. The bill also makes adjustments to the standard deduction, tax brackets, and the estate tax.

list.snippet: No tax on tips and overtime: The bill establishes deductions for tips and overtime pay, with phaseouts for higher earners.
Increased Child Tax Credit: The child tax credit was increased to $2,200 per qualified child.
Additional Senior Deduction: Taxpayers 65 and older are eligible for an additional deduction, with phaseouts for higher earners.
Increased Standard Deduction: The standard deduction was increased and indexed to inflation.
Estate Tax: The amount of assets that can be inherited without triggering the estate tax was increased and indexed to inflation.
SALT Deduction: The bill increased the state and local tax (SALT) itemized deduction.
Vehicle Interest Deduction: A deduction for interest payments on certain vehicles was also included.
Trump Savings Accounts for Children: The bill introduced a new type of IRA for children with a tax credit when opened.
End of Electric Vehicle Credit: The Electric Vehicle Credit is set to end on September 30, 2025.
The bill, known as the "One Big Beautiful Bill," was introduced in the House of Representatives.
It went through committee markups and was amended before being passed by the House.
The Senate also passed the bill after some adjustments.
President Trump signed the bill into law on July 4, 2025.
The bill is intended to spur economic growth and job creation, according to the White House.
It is also designed to provide tax relief to working and middle-class families.
The bill's provisions are expected to have a significant impact on individuals, families, and businesses.
